scope: Formative authoring feasibility over an existing synthetic BI source with raw tables, metric views and saved SQL exports; not raw-table-only metric invention, operational recurrence, a human usability panel, notification delivery, comparative superiority or enterprise certification.
brief: Help Harbor Help's Support Operations lead set up a weekly check on priority support resolution SLA misses. Explain the latest available creation-week cohort and what changed; do not confuse first response with resolution. Ask about the intended policy, show a useful first readout, and save the reusable brief. Do not approve, send, schedule or evaluate anything yet.

owner_declarations.owner://support/definition: We mean completed-ticket resolution performance: priority=1 tickets that are resolved, grouped by the UTC week they were created, across all three tiers and all three regions. Use each tier's source-defined elapsed-hour resolution clock, strict greater-than for a miss. Pool misses and eligible counts; don't average tier percentages. First response is a separate clock and population. Open priority backlog and unanswered tickets are useful separate context, not proof that the completed-ticket rate covers every customer experience.
owner_declarations.owner://support/policy: This is a retrospective review of the fixed historical source, not a current-business freshness SLA. Compare the latest available creation-week cohort with the preceding week. With complete coverage in both, notify Support Operations if the pooled resolution miss rate is greater than 20 percent OR has increased by at least 4 percentage points. Otherwise ignore for alerting, while still giving the requested short weekly report. Missing or unknown expected tier/region coverage takes precedence: insufficient_data to the Data Steward, never interpret missing tickets as zero misses. A resumed ingestion interval does not repair a prior gap.
owner_declarations.owner://support/report: For the lead, give the two pooled counts/rates, the percentage-point change, and the most relevant tier or region contribution when supported. Include separate open-backlog context only if useful. State the historical cohort/cutoff and material gap without a wall of jargon. A breakdown is not a causal explanation. Don't make up incident causes or claim all-ticket SLA attainment. Store definitions/policy separately from the dated example values.
owner_declarations.owner://support/delegation: For this synthetic shadow exercise, the analyst may publish its source-linked findings to the one configured local analysis publication and save draft context/cards. That publication is an explicitly delegated input, not a truth certificate. Show the proposed policy/source scope and readout for review. These declarations are not approval of any not-yet-written card and do not authorize sending, scheduling or a decision-provider call.

admission: Independent code/method review, current native fingerprint, complete software checks and matching zero-inference preflight required before inference. Exclusive protocol claim closes cohort before first actor. Treatment first; baseline only after complete treatment with known single-turn CLI usage, unchanged source/method and no provider attempt. No retry, repair, budget increase, pooled cost or transfer of unused allowance. Timeout excludes CLI startup/registry/cleanup. Tool attempts are bounded and visible; model token limits unavailable, token stops only between actors.
fairness: Both keep the same actual SQL MCP tools, owner statements, publication helper and durable working notes. The company source exposes raw tickets AND inspectable source-owned metric views, like an existing BI stack; this is not a raw-table-only metric-invention test. Views compute counts from underlying rows, not final alert decisions or causal findings. Three operator-configured saved queries export the latest two cohorts of resolution, coverage and backlog, without alert thresholds or outcomes; both arms can use that generic SQL export tool and all original SQL. This source preparation is disclosed and not attributed to agent onboarding. Treatment's native catalog contains those sources and an optional analyst publication, so routine cards need not depend on a frontier-written report. Treatment adds the installed skill and actual default-profile native drafting/review/context tools, never full-profile tools or approval/evaluation. Neither opening prompt contains private arithmetic references, a prepared card, target labels or a prepared analytical readout. Source states are final retrospective, not point-in-time history. Fixed order, tiny cohort and conditional baseline make timings/tokens descriptive setup costs only.
acceptance: Retain actual messages, SQL arguments/results, publication, saved notes/card/context and native review. Require known CLI usage and source/method identity before interpreting completion. Separate expert review against raw rows and owner policy must still assess meaning and arithmetic before card approval or a new recurrence study; successful authoring is not analytical correctness. Missing, failed and censored outputs remain outcomes, not repaired scores.
